speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience fever or chills, and does the pain radiate from your flank down toward your groin? Have you noticed any difficulty urinating or changes in urine flow?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of recurrent UTIs and current symptoms, I need to rule out stones or infection. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_with_culture. REQUEST TEST: CT_urography.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance Reddish, WBC 10-20 /HPF, RBC Too numerous to count, Nitrites Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Positive. CT Urography not performed; Intravenous Pyelogram performed with findings: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging reveals multiple cysts in the medullary collecting ducts, which is highly characteristic of medullary sponge kidney. This condition often presents with hematuria and recurrent UTIs due to urinary stasis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney
